page_subtitle: 知之為知之，練功前先瞭解練什麼
page_subtitle_en: Know What You Practice. Practice with Purpose.

methods.title: 一、華陀導引氣功
methods.desc:
華陀導引炁(氣)功。是東漢神醫華陀配合中醫學理、五行運化法則所創之養生導引炁功，流傳迄今已達一千八百餘年。

整套動作模仿自然界中熊、猴、虎、鹿、鳥等動物的運動型態，伸展肢體並配合吐納，不憋氣、不硬彎曲，把拳經中「發於腿，主宰於腰，形於指」活用其中。

簡單來說，可以將氣功理解為一種養生保健操，經年累月的持續練習不但可以使身體更加舒暢，更能養好精氣神。
methods.desc_en:
Hua Tuo Daoyin Qigong is a health-nourishing practice created over 1,800 years ago by the legendary Eastern Han physician Hua Tuo, based on Traditional Chinese Medicine principles and Five Elements theory.

The routine mimics the movements of five animals—bear, monkey, tiger, deer, and bird. It combines physical stretching with natural breath regulation—without holding your breath or forcing bends—applying the classic martial principle: 'rooted in the legs, directed by the waist, and expressed through the fingers.'

In short, think of Qigong as a wellness exercise. Consistent practice over time relaxes the body and enhances your essential vitality and spirit.
methods.plain_desc:
華佗導引氣功，相傳為東漢名醫華佗所創，是一套結合肢體運動與呼吸調節的傳統養生功法，至今已有一千八百多年的歷史。

整套功法取法自然，動作模仿熊、猴、虎、鹿、鳥等鳥獸伸展、活動身體的姿態，透過輕鬆的肢體運動配合自然呼吸，讓身體逐漸活動開來。練習時不需要憋氣，也不要求勉強彎曲身體，而是以自然、柔和的方式完成每個動作。

簡單來說，可以把氣功想成一套結合伸展、活動與呼吸的養生運動。持續練習，不僅能幫助身體放鬆、活動筋骨，也能在一呼一吸之間，讓身心慢慢沉澱下來。
methods.plain_desc_en:
Hua Tuo Daoyin Qigong is a traditional health-cultivation practice combining movement and breath control, said to be created by the famed Eastern Han doctor Hua Tuo over 1,800 years ago.

Inspired by nature, the movements imitate the stretches and motions of five animals: the bear, monkey, tiger, deer, and bird. Through gentle movements paired with natural breathing, your body gradually warms up. There is no need to hold your breath or force any bends; each movement is completed in a natural and smooth manner.

Simply put, Qigong is a wellness routine that blends stretching, mobility, and breathwork. Consistent practice relaxes the muscles, improves flexibility, and helps settle your mind and body with every breath.

methods.title: 二、太極拳
methods.desc:
太極拳又名十三勢，係結合身法之八法（掤、捋、擠、按、採、挒、肘、靠），和步法之五行（左顧、右盼、前進、後退、中定）合而稱之。

傳統太極拳係以楊式太極的舒展大方架式為主，合於「方圓並用」「虛實兼收」「陰陽相濟」「並符人體「升降、開合、吞吐」之生理自然之勢，以達氣靜神恬、氣血舒暢之太極意境。

輔以拳法攻防、沾黏連隨、借力使力，讓養生功法注入技撃概念，進而將太極陰陽、虛實、剛柔、動靜等相對理論，轉化為調養身心的哲學實踐，極具內涵。
methods.desc_en:
Tai Chi Chuan, also known as the Thirteen Postures, combines eight body techniques (Ward Off, Rollback, Press, Push, Pluck, Split, Elbow Strike, Shoulder Strike) with five steps (Forward, Backward, Look Left, Glance Right, Central Equilibrium).

Our traditional style mainly draws from Yang-style Tai Chi—expansive and graceful. It embodies squareness and roundness, substantiality and insubstantiality, and the balance of Yin and Yang, mirroring natural body rhythms (rising/falling, opening/closing) to reach a peaceful mind and smooth internal energy flow.

Integrating martial applications like stickiness, connection, and yielding to redirect force, it bridges health cultivation with practical defense, transforming philosophies of Yin-Yang, hard-soft, and movement-tranquility into mind-body practice.
methods.plain_desc:
太極拳又稱「十三勢」，由八種身法與五種步法組成。八種身法包括掤、捋、擠、按、採、挒、肘、靠，五種步法則包含進、退、顧、盼與中定。這些動作與步法相互配合，構成太極拳基本的身體運用方式。

本社團以楊式太極拳為主要練習內容，動作舒展大方、連貫柔和，講求身體的開合、虛實與動靜變化。練習時配合自然呼吸與身體的節奏，使動作不僵不硬，在持續的運動中達到放鬆身心、活動筋骨的效果。

太極拳不只是養生運動，也是一套具有攻防概念的武術。透過沾黏連隨、借力使力等拳法原理，學習如何感受對方的力量與動向，並以身體的協調與步法加以應對。

從養生到武術，再從武術回到身心調養，太極拳將陰陽、虛實、剛柔、動靜等傳統思想融入日常練習之中。
methods.plain_desc_en:
Tai Chi Chuan is also called the 'Thirteen Postures,' comprising eight body techniques and five steps. The techniques are Ward Off, Rollback, Press, Push, Pluck, Split, Elbow, and Shoulder Strike; the steps cover advance, retreat, left, right, and central balance. Together, they form the fundamental mechanics of Tai Chi movement.

Our club primarily practices Yang-style Tai Chi, characterized by open, flowing, and gentle postures that emphasize opening/closing, weight shifts, and fluid transitions. Paired with natural breathing and rhythm, the movements remain supple, allowing you to relax the mind and loosen joints through continuous practice.

Beyond health, Tai Chi is a martial art with combat principles. By mastering techniques like sticking, following, and redirecting force, you learn to sense incoming energy and respond with body coordination and footwork.

Connecting health, martial technique, and mental discipline, Tai Chi seamlessly integrates concepts like Yin-Yang, hardness-softness, and stillness into daily movement.

methods.title: 三、太祖棍
methods.desc:
太祖棍法相傳由宋太祖趙匡胤所創，所謂「一條盤龍棍打下趙氏江山」，可見太祖棍法之精妙。

太祖棍法強調欄、拿、扎、戳、挑、扣、撥、劈等動作，運腕靈活，既開合有度，又剛猛迅捷，步穩身靈，騰挪側閃，上挑撩擊快如狂風，下劈砸擊準如利劍，力發於腿，以身帶棍，身棍合一，期以最有效率方式，克敵制勝。

本套太祖棍法，除有單人棍法套路外，也有基於攻防目的，而有十八棍的雙人棍法對練，對練習者而言，可以養成敵我攻防意識。
methods.desc_en:
Legend has it that Taizu Staff was created by Emperor Taizu of Song (Zhao Kuangyin), famous for the saying: 'A single Dragon Staff secured the Song Dynasty.'

This style emphasizes flexible wrist movements and techniques like block, parry, thrust, strike, flick, hook, deflect, and chop. Balancing open and tight movements, it combines powerful speed with agile footwork and evasive maneuvers. Power originates from the legs and transfers through the body into the staff, uniting practitioner and weapon for maximum efficiency.

In addition to solo forms, our routine includes the Eighteen Staffs partner drill to build practical combat awareness and defensive timing.
methods.plain_desc:
太祖棍法相傳由宋太祖趙匡胤所創，民間更有「一條盤龍棍打下趙氏江山」的說法，足見其在傳統武術中的特色與地位。

太祖棍法以棍法的攻防變化為核心，包含欄、拿、扎、戳、挑、扣、撥、劈等多種棍法。動作講求手腕靈活、步伐穩健，並透過身體的轉動帶動棍法，使動作在開合之間兼具力量與速度。練習時需要靈活移動、閃避與進退，培養身體的協調性與對距離、時機的掌握。

本套太祖棍法除了單人棍法套路外，還有以實際攻防為基礎的十八棍雙人對練。透過兩人一攻一守的練習，除了熟悉棍法招式，也能進一步培養對攻防變化的判斷與應對能力。
methods.plain_desc_en:
Taizu Staff is traditionally attributed to Emperor Taizu of Song. Folk legend says 'a single Dragon Staff built the Song Empire,' highlighting its iconic standing in traditional martial arts.

Centered on combat adaptations, the method incorporates key techniques such as blocking, capturing, thrusting, picking, deflecting, and chopping. It calls for wrist flexibility, stable footwork, and generating staff force through torso rotation, striking a balance between power and speed. Practice builds agility, coordination, and a keen sense of distance and timing.

Alongside solo forms, our curriculum features the 18-Move Partner Sparring Drill. Practicing attack and defense with a partner builds tactical judgment and reflex responses to dynamic moves.

methods.title: 四、太極劍
methods.desc:
太極劍為楊家專長兵器之一，動作温和柔順，以太極拳為功底，先開展後緊湊，輾轉攻防。

以腰腿為主，意氣為輔。以氣運身，以意運劍，意先身後，身隨劍走。虛實分清，剛柔相濟。手以臂靈腕活為宗，步以矯捷輕靈為尚。且需氣整神凝，週身貫串，勁由內發，以達身與劍合、劍與意合之境。
methods.desc_en:
Tai Chi Sword is a signature weapon form of Yang-style Tai Chi. Rooted in Tai Chi Chuan principles, its movements transition smoothly between expansive opening stances and tight defensive maneuvers.

Driven by the waist and legs and guided by intent and breath, energy moves the body while mind directs the sword. It demands supple arms, nimble wrists, quick footwork, and a distinct balance of soft and hard. Internal energy flows continuously, unifying body, sword, and mind into one seamlessly aligned state.
methods.plain_desc:
太極劍是楊家太極拳的重要兵器之一。劍法動作柔和流暢，以太極拳的身法與步法為基礎，在舒展與收斂之間轉換，結合進攻與防守，展現太極拳靈活、連貫的特色。

練習太極劍時，以腰腿帶動全身，配合呼吸與專注，讓身體與劍的動作保持協調。步伐講求輕巧靈活，手腕與手臂則需要保持柔軟，使劍隨身轉、身隨劍行。透過對虛實、快慢與剛柔的掌握，逐漸培養身體與兵器之間的協調，最終達到「身劍合一」的境界。
methods.plain_desc_en:
Tai Chi Sword is an essential weapon form within Yang-style Tai Chi. Built upon foundational body postures and footwork, its gentle, flowing techniques shift between open stretches and precise defense, exemplifying the agile essence of Tai Chi.

Practicing Tai Chi Sword involves leading the body through the waist and legs while coordinating breath and focus. Footwork stays light and agile, while wrists and arms remain relaxed, allowing the blade to follow body turns. Mastering rhythm, balance, and force harmony ultimately leads to true unity between practitioner and sword.
